name: genotoxicity-structural-alerts
licence: CC0-1.0 (public domain dedication) — first-party SMARTS, ported from Chemclaw3's `chemclaw.science.safety`, which is MIT-licensed content of the same owner. The alert *concepts* are published science attributed per row (see retrieved_from); the patterns encoding them were written in that repository.
retrieved_from: Ported from Chemclaw3's `src/chemclaw/science/safety/genotox_alerts.yaml`, since extended here with the `vinyl-sulfone` row (an alkylating motif the `michael-acceptor` explanation claimed and its pattern could not match). The alert set each row cites: Ashby & Tennant, Mutat. Res. 1988, 204, 17 (structural alerts for DNA reactivity — N-nitroso, epoxide, aziridine); Benigni & Bossa, Chem. Rev. 2011, 111, 2507 (structural alerts for mutagenicity — nitroaromatic, primary aromatic amine, aromatic azo, alkyl halide, sulfonate/sulfate ester, Michael acceptor, vinyl sulfone); ICH M7(R2), 2023, Assessment and Control of DNA Reactive (Mutagenic) Impurities; and the EMA nitrosamine Article 5(3) referral outcome, 2020, for the nitrosamine formation route. Nothing is fetched at runtime and no address here is read by any code.
description: Ten DNA-reactive structural alerts (N-nitroso, nitroaromatic, primary aromatic amine, aromatic azo, epoxide, aziridine, mono-functional alkyl halide, alkyl sulfonate/sulfate ester, alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl, vinyl sulfone) plus one formation pair — a nitrosatable amine meeting a nitrosating agent — each with the motif it names, why it is an alert, and the published alert set it comes from. NO ROW CARRIES A CLASS, A LIMIT OR A PURGE FACTOR, deliberately: an ICH M7 class, an acceptable intake and a purge factor are outputs of a model (two complementary (Q)SARs plus an Ames corpus and expert review) that this system does not have. A flag is an alert for expert assessment; an empty result is ten patterns not matching, not a negative mutagenicity prediction.
